note: The level 1 (V3) prompts. Level 1 is one attempt (attemptsOne); the attempt prompts below are kept for the record. {N}, {PREV}, {TRIES}, {STROKES} and {MIN} are filled in by bench/scripts/v3.mjs. done is added when the model may end early. Every attempt is a fresh worktree and a fresh model session: `next` is the whole first message of attempt 2 and later.
attemptsExact: This run has exactly {TRIES} attempts. After attempt 1 the harness shows you your painting next to the target and asks for attempt 2.
attemptsUpTo: This run has up to {TRIES} attempts. After each attempt the harness shows you your painting next to the target and asks for the next one; you may instead declare the painting done.
first: Read bench/BRIEF.md in this directory and do attempt 1 as it says. The target crop is attached. Work without asking questions; nobody will answer.
next: Read bench/BRIEF.md in this directory; this is attempt {N} of {OF}. The target crop is attached, and is at the path the brief gives. You painted attempt {PREV} in an earlier session ({STROKES} strokes, {MIN} minutes); this is a fresh folder and a fresh session, and nothing of that session is here except bench/attempts/a{PREV}/: its scripts, final.png, frames, stats.json and compare.png (the target on the left, your painting on the right). That folder is read-only and for reference: open compare.png and look, and read the script to see what you did. Now paint attempt {N} on a fresh sheet with the same budget: up to 3 paintings, no limit on strokes (a far safety stop ends the session after {LIMIT_MIN} minutes). You decide what to change. First write one line to bench/attempts/a{N}-changed.txt: what you are changing and why. Then paint, end with kit.finish, and stop. Work without asking questions; nobody will answer.
done: If you judge the painting done, and another attempt would not make it better, do not paint: write one line to bench/DONE saying why, and stop.
attemptsOne: This run is one attempt: one fresh session. Your script may run at most 3 paintings (each run that lays a mark is one); the painting of your last completed run is the one that counts.
